event: Nala says: "Hi there, would you mind pointing me in the direction of your parents?"
The boy's face splits in a grin. "Pointing? I'll take you. My da's the reeve of Harrow, he is."
He swings the switch and turns the whole flock back east, geese squawking at the change.
"I'm Hob. Da's Aldous Crane. He keeps the roll. Everyone has to answer to him."

memory.fact: The goose boy is Hob, son of Aldous Crane, Harrow's reeve.
The goose boy is Hob, son of Aldous Crane, Harrow's reeve.
The reeve keeps Harrow's roll, and everyone in Harrow has to answer to him.
The reeve keeps Harrow's roll, and everyone in Harrow has to answer to him.
Harrow's reeve is Aldous Crane.

event: He doesn't wait for her name; he's onto the dogs, all howling at once round three o'clock.
"And the air hummed, like bees in a wall. And all the crows went up off the Mile at once."

memory.fact: Round three on day one, every dog about Harrow howled at once and the air hummed like bees.
Round three on day one, every dog about Harrow howled at once and the air hummed like bees.
When the dogs howled, all the crows went up off Harrow Mile at once.
When the dogs howled, all the crows went up off Harrow Mile at once.
Folk in the fields felt the air hum then, and the crows rose all at once from Harrow Mile.

event: "Mam says it's nothing. Da went quiet, which means it's something."

memory.fact: Hob's mam says the howling and hum are nothing; his da went quiet over them.
Hob's mam says the howling and hum are nothing; his da went quiet over them.

event: The road runs down into the village; the sun slips under the rise and the light goes grey-gold.
Hob steers the geese round the back of a long thatched alehouse with a sheaf painted on its sign.

memory.fact: A long thatched building in Harrow has a sheaf of grain painted on its sign and smells of stew.
A long thatched building in Harrow has a sheaf of grain painted on its sign and smells of stew.

event: Mutton stew smells through its back shutters; he pens the geese in a wattle fold, talking all along.

memory.fact: Hob pens the geese in a woven wattle fold behind the building with the sheaf sign.
Hob pens the geese in a woven wattle fold behind the building with the sheaf sign.
On day one's evening the Sheaf's hearth has a pot of mutton stew on it.
On day one's evening the Sheaf's hearth has a pot of mutton stew on it.
Hob must pen the geese in the fold behind the Sheaf before he may go home.

event: Then out onto the green: a well, a tall bell post, cottages of daub and thatch all round.

memory.fact: Its cottages are wattle, daub and thatch around a green with a well and a bell post.
Its cottages are wattle, daub and thatch around a green with a well and a bell post.
Harrow Green is the open grass at the middle of the village, with the well and the bell post.
Harrow Green is the open grass at the middle of the village, with the well and the bell post.

event: An old woman sits by her door shelling beans into her lap; she squints their way and sees little.

memory.fact: An old woman shells beans by her door on the green, squinting like one who can't see well.
An old woman shells beans by her door on the green, squinting like one who can't see well.
On day one's evening Old Nan sits by her door on the green, shelling beans.

event: A man at a gate stops with a bucket; two women in a doorway lean their heads together.
Nala's bare feet go quiet on the grass of the green; every eye on it follows her.

memory.fact: Every eye on Harrow green followed barefoot Nala as Hob led her across it at dusk.
Every eye on Harrow green followed barefoot Nala as Hob led her across it at dusk.

event: Hob marches her to a house on the green's east side, stone-footed, by the bell post.

memory.fact: The Cranes live in the stone-footed house on the green's east side, by the bell post.
The Cranes live in the stone-footed house on the green's east side, by the bell post.

event: He bangs the door with the switch. "Da! I found a lady on the road! She's got no shoes!"
The door opens: a lean man of fifty, grey at the temples, napkin in hand, supper behind him.

memory.fact: Aldous Crane is a lean man of about fifty, grey at the temples.
Aldous Crane is a lean man of about fifty, grey at the temples.
On day one's evening Aldous and Bess are at home, supper on the board, waiting on Hob.

event: He looks at her face and goes still, the napkin halfway to the table.
Something crosses his face, fast; he looks harder, then at the dusk behind her, then back.

changes.note: The reeve sees a face he knows on a stranger, and it raises his guard by three

memory.fact: Aldous went still at the sight of Nala's face, looked harder, then glanced at the dusk behind her.
Aldous went still at the sight of Nala's face, looked harder, then glanced at the dusk behind her.

event: Behind him a stout woman with a ladle peers past his shoulder, frowning at Nala's bare feet.

memory.fact: A stout woman with a ladle in the Cranes' house frowned at Nala's bare feet.
A stout woman with a ladle in the Cranes' house frowned at Nala's bare feet.

event: The man speaks slow and careful. "Evening, mistress."
"Your name, if you'd give it. Where's your home, and what's your business in Harrow?"

memory.fact: At his door Aldous asked Nala her name, her home and her business in Harrow.
At his door Aldous asked Nala her name, her home and her business in Harrow.
Aldous meets a stranger at his door, asks name, home and business, then asks for a road token.
